Geofence path: PendingIntent broadcast -> TaskBroadcastReceiver -> TaskService.handleIntent -> GeofencingTaskConsumer.didReceiveBroadcast -> scheduleJob (JobScheduler, 60 s override deadline) -> TaskJobService -> didExecuteJob -> TaskService.executeTask -> headless loader if no task manager. Boot/replace restore runs inside the TaskService constructor when the static task map is null. Q8: pinned changelogs end at 18.0.10 / 12.0.6; later versions cannot be listed offline (no network fetch done).

facts.fact: Q1 task-manager manifest also declares meta-data expo.modules.taskManager.oneAppId=true.
Q2 TaskBroadcastReceiver.onReceive builds a new TaskService(applicationContext) and calls handleIntent(intent) synchronously; no goAsync, no foreground service, no wakelock in this class.

Q2 restoreTasks() is invoked from the TaskService constructor only when the repository's static task map does not yet exist (tasksExist() is sTasks != null), i.e. first TaskService in a fresh process.
evidence: TM/repository/ManagedTasksAndEventsRepository.java:58-65 — tasksExist() return sTasks != null; createTasks() sTasks = new HashMap<>()

facts.fact: Q2 persisted state: SharedPreferences file 'TaskManagerModule'; one key per appScopeKey holding a JSON string {appUrl, tasks:{<name>:{name, consumerClass, consumerVersion, options}}}. readPersistedTasks skips entries lacking appUrl or non-empty tasks.

Q2 restoreTasks per task: Class.forName(consumerClass); registers via internalRegisterTask only if currentConsumerVersion == saved consumerVersion; otherwise logs a warning and skips; ClassNotFound/NPE skipped; then persists the app's surviving tasks (dropping unrestorable ones). getConsumerVersion reads a static field VERSION, returns 0 if absent; TaskConsumer.VERSION = 0.
evidence: TM/TaskService.java:569-571 — Log.w 'has version ... not compatible with the saved version'
TM/TaskService.java:581 — persistTasksForAppScopeKey after loop ('unregister tasks that couldn't be restored')

facts.fact: Q2 internalRegisterTask constructs the consumer and calls consumer.didRegister(task); for the geofencing consumer didRegister calls startGeofencing (addGeofences to Play services), for the location consumer startLocationUpdates then maybeStartForegroundService. So on BOOT/REPLACED the geofence is re-added and location updates re-requested in the receiver's process; no JS runs at this point.
evidence: TM/TaskService.java:455-469 — consumer = newInstance(context, utils); new Task(...); consumer.didRegister(task)

facts.fact: Q2 handleIntent for non-INTENT_ACTION broadcasts (BOOT_COMPLETED etc.) only iterates consumers and calls didReceiveBroadcast where canReceiveCustomBroadcast(action) is true; default is false and neither location consumer overrides it (no override found in expo-location android). So the boot broadcast's useful effect is the TaskService construction/restoreTasks, not a consumer callback.
evidence: grep canReceiveCustomBroadcast in expo-location-18.0.10/package/android — no matches

facts.fact: Q2 handleIntent for INTENT_ACTION reads appId/taskName from the intent data URI; if the consumer is not found it logs 'Task or consumer not found.' and cancels the pending intent for that task; data URI null returns silently.
Q3 PendingIntent: getBroadcast(requestCode 5055, Intent(INTENT_ACTION, TaskBroadcastReceiver) with data URI ?appId=<scopeKey>&taskName=<name>, flags UPDATE_CURRENT | FLAG_MUTABLE on API>=31).
evidence: TM/TaskManagerUtils.java:185-202 — appendQueryParameter appId/taskName; PendingIntent.getBroadcast(... flags | mutableFlag)

facts.fact: Q3 scheduleJob -> updateOrScheduleJob: lowest unused job id; if a pending job already belongs to the task, merges the new data into it (createJobInfoByAddingData) else creates a new JobInfo; every JobInfo is setMinimumLatency(0) and setOverrideDeadline(60 000 ms) with no constraints (no network/idle/charging set).

Q3 TaskJobService.onStartJob builds TaskService and returns handleJob; onStopJob returns cancelJob. handleJob returns consumer.didExecuteJob(...) (async=true for both location consumers); if async it posts finishJobAfterTimeout(15000) on a new Handler. If consumer not found it returns false (job ends).
evidence: TM/TaskService.java:318-343 — isAsyncJob = consumer.didExecuteJob(...); finishJobAfterTimeout(jobService, params, MAX_TASK_EXECUTION_TIME_MS)

facts.fact: Q3 finishJobAfterTimeout only posts a Runnable that calls jobService.jobFinished(params,false) after the timeout. It does not cancel the pending task callback, does not stop/destroy the React instance, does not stop the JS task. The headless app teardown is separate: when notifyTaskFinished removes the last event for the app it posts invalidateAppRecord after 2000 ms.

Q3 TaskService.executeTask: builds event body (eventId); registers the callback in static sTaskCallbacks; if a TaskManager for the appScopeKey exists (non-headless map first, then headless map) it calls taskManager.executeTaskWithBody immediately; otherwise it queues the body in the repository events and calls getAppLoader().loadApp(context, Params(appScopeKey, task.getAppUrl()), alreadyRunning no-op, callback).
evidence: TM/TaskService.java:372-410 — taskManager != null -> executeTaskWithBody; else putEventForAppScopeKey + loadApp(...)
TM/TaskService.java:360-381 — getTaskManager picks sTaskManagers (foreground) before sHeadlessTaskManagers (see getTaskManager at ~line 553-562)

facts.fact: Q3 loader failure handling: if loadApp callback reports success=false, events are removed and unregisterAllTasksForAppScopeKey is called ('Host unreachable? Unregister all tasks'); AppConfigurationError unregisters that task and removes events.

Q3 RNHeadlessAppLoader.loadApp: only if appRecords (its own static map keyed by appScopeKey, filled only when its own listener fires) lacks the key does it register a ReactInstanceEventListener and post reactHost.start() (new arch) or createReactContextInBackground() (old arch) on the main looper; if the key is present it runs alreadyRunning and does nothing else. It does not consult whether an Activity-hosted instance exists; it throws IllegalStateException if the Application is not a ReactApplication. The callback(true) fires from onReactContextInitialized; no failure callback path exists in this class.
evidence: CORE/adapters/react/apploader/RNHeadlessAppLoader.kt:26-66 — if (!appRecords.containsKey(...)) { addReactInstanceEventListener; Handler(mainLooper).post { reactHost.start() | createReactContextInBackground() } } else alreadyRunning?.run()
CORE/adapters/react/apploader/RNHeadlessAppLoader.kt:67-69 — throw IllegalStateException("Your application must implement ReactApplication")

facts.fact: Q3 invalidateApp destroys the React instance/host only if lifecycleState == BEFORE_CREATE (not bound to an Activity), then notifies destroyed and removes the appRecord; if an Activity owns it, it is not destroyed but the appRecord is still removed. isRunning is true if an appRecord exists (new arch).
evidence: CORE/adapters/react/apploader/RNHeadlessAppLoader.kt:112-118 — isRunning: appRecords[key] ?: return false; new arch return true

TM/TaskService.java:238-252 — setTaskManager replays getEvents(appScopeKey) then removeEvents

evidence: TM/TaskService.java:383-392 — if (sEvents.get(appScopeKey)==null) { appEvents=new...; sEvents.put } else { appEvents = new ArrayList<>(); appEvents.add(eventId); }

facts.fact: Q4 geofence request: INITIAL_TRIGGER_ENTER | INITIAL_TRIGGER_EXIT; each geofence setExpirationDuration(NEVER_EXPIRE); transition types = ENTER if notifyOnEnter (default true) | EXIT if notifyOnExit (default true); no loitering delay or DWELL is requested; requestId = region identifier or random UUID.

Q4 on event.hasError() the consumer maps the code (NOT_AVAILABLE -> 'Geofencing not available.', TOO_MANY_GEOFENCES, TOO_MANY_PENDING_INTENTS, else 'Unknown geofencing error.') and calls mTask?.execute(null, error) directly, which goes TaskService.executeTask -> JS (loading the headless app if needed); it does NOT go through scheduleJob/JobService, does not re-add geofences, and does not call startGeofencing again. A null GeofencingEvent is logged and ignored.
evidence: LOC/taskConsumers/GeofencingTaskConsumer.kt:61-71 — fromIntent null -> return; hasError -> getErrorString; mTask?.execute(null, error); return
TM/Task.java:49-51 — execute(data, error, callback) -> mService.executeTask(this, data, error, callback)

facts.fact: Q4 transition handling: state INSIDE for ENTER/DWELL, OUTSIDE for EXIT; for each triggering geofence found in the in-memory mRegions map, one scheduleJob(context, mTask, [data]) call is made (data = eventType + region bundle). If triggeringGeofences is null it returns; geofences whose requestId is not in mRegions are skipped silently. mRegions is rebuilt only in startGeofencing.
evidence: LOC/taskConsumers/GeofencingTaskConsumer.kt:124-137 — mRegions = HashMap(); populated per region in startGeofencing

facts.fact: Q4 didExecuteJob (geofencing): for each queued item calls task.execute(bundle,null){ jobService.jobFinished(params,false) } and returns true; the callback is created per item, so the first item to finish calls jobFinished for the whole job. mTask null returns false.
evidence: LOC/taskConsumers/GeofencingTaskConsumer.kt:93-110 — for (item in data) { task.execute(bundle, null) { jobService.jobFinished(params, false) } } return true

facts.fact: Q4 startGeofencing returns silently (no throw, no JS event) if no location provider (GPS or NETWORK) is enabled; it swallows SecurityException from addGeofences with a log; it does not attach success/failure listeners to addGeofences, so an async addGeofences failure is not observed. A bad region field throws GeofencingException.
evidence: LOC/taskConsumers/GeofencingTaskConsumer.kt:148-156 — mGeofencingClient?.addGeofences(request, pendingIntent) inside try/catch SecurityException (no listeners)

facts.fact: Q4 GeofencingTaskConsumer defines no VERSION field and overrides setOptions to stopGeofencing() then startGeofencing(). LocationTaskConsumer also defines no VERSION field (inherits TaskConsumer.VERSION=0 via getDeclaredField miss -> 0).
evidence: grep VERSION LOC/taskConsumers/*.kt — only Build.VERSION.SDK_INT at LocationTaskConsumer.kt:165

facts.fact: Q5 option mapping: LocationRequest built from accuracy-derived default interval/distance, overridden by timeInterval (ms) and distanceInterval (m); minUpdateInterval and maxUpdateDelay are both set to the interval; priority from accuracy (BestForNavigation/Highest/High -> HIGH_ACCURACY; Balanced/Low -> BALANCED_POWER_ACCURACY; Lowest -> LOW_POWER). Accuracy defaults: Lowest 3000 m/10000 ms; Low 1000/5000; Balanced 100/3000; High 50/2000; Highest 25/1000; BestForNavigation 0/500.

Q5 LocationOptions Android fields read for the task consumer: accuracy, distanceInterval, timeInterval, mayShowUserSettingsDialog. LocationTaskOptions fields: deferredUpdatesDistance, deferredUpdatesInterval, deferredUpdatesTimeout, foregroundService. No Kotlin field exists for pausesUpdatesAutomatically, showsBackgroundLocationIndicator or activityType in these records; deferredUpdatesTimeout is declared but not read by LocationTaskConsumer.
evidence: LOC/records/LocationArguments.kt:21-25 — LocationOptions: accuracy, distanceInterval, mayShowUserSettingsDialog, timeInterval
LOC/records/LocationArguments.kt:42-46 — LocationTaskOptions: deferredUpdatesDistance, deferredUpdatesInterval, deferredUpdatesTimeout, foregroundService

facts.fact: Q5 deferral logic: while the host is resumed (mIsHostPaused=false) every location is reported immediately; while paused, locations are buffered and reported only when (newest.time - oldest.time) >= deferredUpdatesInterval AND accumulated distance >= deferredUpdatesDistance (both read via options). mIsHostPaused starts true. Reporting calls scheduleJob (not direct JS). A static sLastTimestamp drops locations with time <= last scheduled.

Q5 foreground-service start: maybeStartForegroundService returns without starting (log warning 'cannot be started while the app is in the background!') if SDK<O or !AppForegroundedSingleton.isForegrounded; it also returns if mTask is null, if option 'foregroundService' is absent, and otherwise startForegroundService + bindService(BIND_AUTO_CREATE); if mService already exists it re-calls startForeground with new options; if mService exists but option removed it stops the service. location updates (requestLocationUpdates) are started independently of the foreground-service check in didRegister/setOptions.
evidence: LOC/taskConsumers/LocationTaskConsumer.kt:180-223 — mService != null && !useForegroundService -> stop; mService == null -> startForegroundService/bindService; else startForeground(options)

facts.fact: Q5 AppForegroundedSingleton.isForegrounded is set true in LocationModule OnActivityEntersForeground and false in OnActivityEntersBackground (static in-process flag). LocationTaskService.onStartCommand returns START_REDELIVER_INTENT; killServiceOnDestroy (default false) is passed as extra 'killService' and, only when true, onTaskRemoved calls stop(); the service notification channel (appId:taskName) is created IMPORTANCE_LOW if missing. startForeground(...) is only called from the ServiceConnection after bind.
evidence: LOC/LocationModule.kt:313-319 — OnActivityEntersForeground { isForegrounded = true }; OnActivityEntersBackground { = false }
LOC/services/LocationTaskService.kt:34-41 — mKillService = extras.getBoolean("killService", false); return START_REDELIVER_INTENT

facts.fact: Q5 hasStartedLocationUpdatesAsync returns mTaskManager.taskHasConsumerOfClass(taskName, LocationTaskConsumer) i.e. task registered with that consumer class (task != null && consumer instanceOf); returns false if mTaskService == null. It does not test the foreground service or the Play-services request. hasStartedGeofencingAsync additionally throws LocationBackgroundUnauthorizedException when background permission is missing.

Q6 second start on a registered task: TaskService.registerTask, if a task with that name exists and its consumer is an instance of the requested class, only updates task options and calls task.getConsumer().setOptions(options) (no new consumer); then persists. For LocationTaskConsumer setOptions = stopLocationUpdates(); startLocationUpdates(); maybeStartForegroundService() (so the foreground-service foregrounded check runs again). For GeofencingTaskConsumer setOptions = stopGeofencing(); startGeofencing(). Otherwise internalRegisterTask creates a new consumer.
evidence: TM/TaskService.java:93-106 — task already exists: task.setOptions; task.getConsumer().setOptions(options); else internalRegisterTask; persist

facts.fact: Q6 stopLocationUpdates/stopGeofencing remove the Play-services registration using the saved mPendingIntent and cancel it; after a process restart mPendingIntent is null until didRegister/startX creates it, so the stop uses the fields of the current consumer instance only.

Q7 LocationModule.startLocationUpdatesAsync (lines 255-277): shouldUseForegroundService = options.foregroundService != null; (1) if isMissingForegroundPermissions() (neither FINE nor COARSE granted) throw LocationBackgroundUnauthorizedException; (2) if !shouldUseForegroundService && isMissingBackgroundPermissions() (SDK>=Q and no ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION) throw LocationBackgroundUnauthorizedException; (3) if !AppForegroundedSingleton.isForegrounded && foregroundService != null throw ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException; (4) if !hasForegroundServicePermissions() throw ForegroundServicePermissionsException; then registerTask(taskName, LocationTaskConsumer, options.toMutableMap()). hasForegroundServicePermissions: API>=34 needs FOREGROUND_SERVICE and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION granted; API>=28 needs FOREGROUND_SERVICE; else true; it is evaluated even when no foregroundService option was passed.

Q7 startGeofencingAsync checks only isMissingBackgroundPermissions() (throw LocationBackgroundUnauthorizedException) then registerTask(taskName, GeofencingTaskConsumer, options.toMap()); no foreground-permission, provider-enabled or foreground-state check. Exception messages: 'Not authorized to use background location services'; 'Couldn't start the foreground service. Foreground service cannot be started when the application is in the background'; '...Foreground service permissions were not found in the manifest'.
evidence: LOC/LocationModule.kt:288-295 — startGeofencingAsync: if (isMissingBackgroundPermissions()) throw ...; registerTask(... GeofencingTaskConsumer ...)

anomalies: TaskService.executeTask else-branch creates a fresh local appEvents list for the second concurrent event and never stores it in sEvents (TM/TaskService.java:383-392).

Geofence error path mTask.execute(null, error) bypasses scheduleJob/JobService so there is no JobScheduler job, no 15 s timer and no jobFinished on that path (LOC/taskConsumers/GeofencingTaskConsumer.kt:66-71).
GeofencingTaskConsumer.didExecuteJob calls jobFinished from the per-item callback inside a loop, so the first finished item finishes the job for all items (GeofencingTaskConsumer.kt:97-105).
addGeofences is called without success/failure listeners; startGeofencing returns silently when no GPS/NETWORK provider is enabled (GeofencingTaskConsumer.kt:120-123, 148-156).
RNHeadlessAppLoader.loadApp decides by its own appRecords map, not by whether an Activity-hosted React instance is running (RNHeadlessAppLoader.kt:27, 64-66).
hasForegroundServicePermissions is checked in startLocationUpdatesAsync even when no foregroundService option is passed (LocationModule.kt:268-270, 720-733).
Pinned changelogs contain nothing past expo-location 18.0.10 / expo-task-manager 12.0.6, so Q8 'later than pinned' entries could not be listed offline.
questions_for_deep_dive: Which expo-location / expo-task-manager releases after 18.0.10 / 12.0.6 changed Android geofencing, headless-job, boot-restore or foreground-service behaviour (requires a network changelog fetch)?

When BOOT_COMPLETED fires and the process starts cold, does LocationTaskConsumer.didRegister at restoreTasks time ever start the foreground service, given AppForegroundedSingleton.isForegrounded is false in a fresh process?

What does the JS side of expo-task-manager (TaskManager.defineTask executor) do with the error object passed on a GEOFENCE_NOT_AVAILABLE event, and does the app's task handler ever re-register the geofence?

How does the Play-services geofence registration (not persisted by Play services across reboot/app update/location-setting toggle) interact with restoreTasks only running when the static task map is null?
